anymd 

 
PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, EPUB, HTML and web pages, images (OCR), audio and video (metadata, subtitles, transcripts). A fast Rust MCP server and CLI that runs on your machine. No API key.
 

 
Need verifiable PDF quote checks and video frames? Get anymd Pro to verify PDF quotes and cite exact video frames offline for US$29 once.
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 

Install · Benchmarks · Tools · CLI · Formats · Docs · Studio · Pro, US$29 once

 
 Formerly pdf-reader-mcp . Migrating from pdf-reader-mcp 
 

 

 A real, unedited terminal recording (asciinema + agg, script ). The last command is Claude Code answering from the PDF through the anymd MCP server. 

 

 

From PyPI: pip install anymd to install the CLI and Python API, or uvx anymd to run the CLI without a separate install.

Also on Homebrew ( brew install sylphxai/tap/anymd ), crates.io ( cargo install anymd ) and Docker ( ghcr.io/sylphxai/anymd ). See every install option.

 
 

 Head to head on the same 38 documents (AgentDocBench score · time for all 38 · output tokens):

- vs Docling: 96.4 vs 93.0 · 11.5 s vs 2,432.4 s · 14% fewer tokens 
- vs Kreuzberg: 96.4 vs 81.7 · 11.5 s vs 16.0 s · 19% fewer tokens 
- vs Unstructured: 96.4 vs 81.2 · 11.5 s vs 346.5 s · 11% fewer tokens 
- vs MarkItDown: 96.4 vs 76.8 · 11.5 s vs 75.6 s · 32% fewer tokens 

 

 Why anymd

 
- Fast. Native Rust converts in parallel, page by page. On the 38 benchmark documents, anymd takes 11.5 s in total; docling 2,432.4 s (212×), markitdown 75.6 s (7×); marker converted 30 of them in 7,104.5 s, against anymd's 4.64 s on the same 30 (1,532×).
 
- Accurate. A layout engine rebuilds words from glyph gaps, puts two-column papers in reading order, and recovers tables, including borderless ones. The text stays exactly as printed, with no glued words and no scrambled columns.
- Lean on tokens. Pages come back as Markdown with citation anchors, a small front-matter header, and compact tables. A token budget and a cursor keep large documents within your agent's context.
- Every format, one call. One tool reads every format listed below. It also accepts web URLs and whole directories, and search looks across all of them.
- Local and private. Nothing is uploaded. OCR uses installed local doc-VLM models or tesseract; transcripts use ffmpeg and bundled Qwen3-ASR. OCR setup and ASR model downloads require explicit opt-in.
- Evidence your agent can show (Pro). anymd Pro checks a PDF quote against the page and area it cites, and returns the exact video frame behind a claim. US$29, one payment.

 Benchmarks

AgentDocBench is an open benchmark for document → Markdown conversion for agents: license-clean documents in 12 categories (math papers, two-column papers, financial tables, forms, scans, CJK, slides, spreadsheets, Word, EPUB, HTML), scored on verbatim sentences, text F1, reading order, and table cells, with time and output tokens. Every tool runs on the same kind of GitHub-hosted runner (4 CPUs):

The generated leaderboard, per-category scores (including where anymd loses), and method are in the benchmark guide. All comparisons puts the seven tools side by side, and head-to-head pages compare anymd with Docling, Kreuzberg, Marker, MarkItDown, pdftotext and Unstructured. The corpus, ground truth, adapters, and raw results are in bench/ , and the Benchmark workflow reruns everything; new tools can join with a single adapter file.

install.title: Install
install.html:
Add anymd to every MCP client on your machine (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code, Claude Desktop, Windsurf, Gemini CLI) with one command:

npx -y @sylphx/anymd setup     # --dry-run to preview, --remove to undo

To set up only some clients, name them: --client cursor,claude-code,codex. The other ids are vscode, vscode-insiders, claude-desktop, windsurf and gemini.

Or add it by hand: every MCP client runs the same command, npx -y @sylphx/anymd. Node 18+ is the only requirement; npm installs the native binary for your platform.

Claude Code
claude mcp add anymd -- npx -y @sylphx/anymd

Or as a plugin, with the anymd skill: /plugin marketplace add SylphxAI/anymd, then /plugin install anymd@anymd.

Codex
codex mcp add anymd -- npx -y @sylphx/anymd

or in ~/.codex/config.toml:

[mcp_servers.anymd]
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "@sylphx/anymd"]
Cursor

or in .cursor/mcp.json:

{ "mcpServers": { "anymd": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@sylphx/anymd"] } } }
VS Code

Install in VS Code with one click, or from a terminal:

code --add-mcp '{"name":"anymd","command":"npx","args":["-y","@sylphx/anymd"]}'

or in .vscode/mcp.json:

{ "servers": { "anymd": { "type": "stdio", "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@sylphx/anymd"] } } }
Claude Desktop

One click: download anymd-<version>.mcpb from the latest release and open it. Or, by hand:

Add to claude_desktop_config.json (Settings → Developer → Edit Config):

{ "mcpServers": { "anymd": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@sylphx/anymd"] } } }
Windsurf, Zed, Cline, and other clients

Any client that speaks MCP over stdio: command npx, args ["-y", "@sylphx/anymd"]. To keep the server inside one folder, add --allow-dir=/path/to/docs.

CLI only
npm install -g @sylphx/anymd     # or run it once with: npx -y @sylphx/anymd <file>

On Windows, macOS and Linux, you can also install from PyPI:

pip install anymd
anymd report.pdf > report.md
# Or run once: uvx anymd report.pdf > report.md

On macOS and Linux, Homebrew is also available:

brew install sylphxai/tap/anymd

Docker (amd64 and arm64):

docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/data" ghcr.io/sylphxai/anymd report.pdf > report.md
docker run -i --rm ghcr.io/sylphxai/anymd        # MCP server on stdio

Or build it from crates.io (Rust 1.95+, CMake and a C++ compiler; doc-VLM OCR and local ASR are included):

cargo install anymd

npm, pip and Docker ship a prebuilt binary, while cargo install compiles one on your machine.
